q.q:

q.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to: DISPARAGE

q.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to: EXTRANEOUS
q.e: Extraneous = not part of the subject; opposite = relevant/essential.

q.q:
Choose the one word that best replaces the phrase:
"A place where bees are kept"

q.q:
Choose the one word that best replaces the phrase:
"Leaving one's own country to settle in another"

q.e: Indirect questions take statement order.

q.q:
Choose the one word that best replaces the phrase:
"A statement that appears contradictory but may be true"

q.e: Garrulous = talking too much about trivial things.

q.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to: SANGUINE
q.e: Sanguine = cheerfully confident about the future.

q.q:
Fill in the blank:
The ______ evidence left the jury no choice but to convict.
q.e: Only 'irrefutable' (cannot be disproved) forces a conviction.

q.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to: OBSEQUIOUS
q.e: Obsequious = excessively eager to please or obey.

q.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to: DEARTH
q.e: Dearth = scarcity; opposite = abundance.

q.q: Let you and ___ go together.
q.e: 'Let' takes an object pronoun.

q.q:
Choose the correct preposition to fill the blank:
Margarine is sometimes used as a substitute ______ butter.
q.e: Substitute for.

q.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to: GREGARIOUS
q.e: Gregarious = fond of company.

q.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to: IMPECUNIOUS
q.e: Impecunious = having little or no money.

q.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to: RECONDITE

q.q: Choose the grammatically correct sentence:
o: Neither the captain nor the players were present at the ceremony.
Neither the captain nor the players was present at the ceremony.
Neither the captain nor the players is present at the ceremony.
Neither the captain or the players were present at the ceremony.
q.e: With 'neither ... nor' the verb agrees with the nearer subject (players).

q.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to: WILY
q.e: Wily = skilled at gaining an advantage deceptively.

q.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to: OPAQUE
q.e: Opaque = hard to understand; not allowing light through.

q.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to: ENERVATE
q.e: Enervate = drain of vitality (a common false friend of 'energise').

q.q:
Choose the one word that best replaces the phrase:
"A person who walks in sleep"
q.e: Somnambulist = sleepwalker.

q.q: Choose the grammatically correct sentence:
o: He is an honest man with an European outlook.
He is an honest man with a European outlook.
He is a honest man with a European outlook.
He is a honest man with an European outlook.
q.e: 'An' goes before a vowel sound (honest has a silent h); 'European' begins with a /j/ sound.

q.q: Choose the pair that has the same relationship as: FLOCK : SHEEP

q.q: Choose the sentence that contains an error:
o: No sooner had I left home than it began to rain.
Hardly had I left home when it began to rain.
Hardly I had left home when it began to rain.
Scarcely had I left home when it began to rain.
q.e: Inversion is needed after 'hardly': "Hardly had I left".

q.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to: ASCETIC

q.q: Statements: All coins are lamps. Some coins are tables. All tables are books. Conclusions: I. All books are lamps.  II. Some books are tables.  III. Some lamps are not tables.  IV. No book is a coin. Which of the conclusions definitely follow(s)?
q.e: Draw all possible Venn diagrams for the three statements; a conclusion follows only if it holds in every one of them.

q.q: Statements: All coins are lamps. No hill is a coin. Some hills are tables. Conclusions: I. Some tables are not lamps.  II. Some hills are not coins.  III. No lamp is a table.  IV. No lamp is a coin. Which of the conclusions definitely follow(s)?
o: Only II, III and IV follow
Only I, II and IV follow
q.e: Draw all possible Venn diagrams for the three statements; a conclusion follows only if it holds in every one of them.

q.q: 5 students Danish, Farah, Imran, Mariam, Sadia each have a test on a different day, from Monday to Friday (one test per day). Imran's test is on either the first or the last day. Mariam's test is held on a day between those of Farah and Danish. Sadia's test is held earlier in the week than Farah's. Danish's and Mariam's tests are on consecutive days. Farah's and Sadia's tests are not on consecutive days. Imran's test is held earlier in the week than Sadia's. On which day is Danish's test held?
q.e: Place the definite clues first (immediate neighbours, ends), then use the 'between' and 'left of' clues to fix the rest; the arrangement is unique.

q.q: Six persons Ali, Danish, Farah, Rabia, Sadia, Salman sit around a circular table, all facing the centre. Sadia is not an immediate neighbour of Salman. Who sits second to the left of Farah?
q.e: Fix one person, then place the others using 'immediate', 'opposite' and 'second to' clues; left and right are taken from the seated person's own view (facing the centre).

q.e: Draw all possible Venn diagrams for the three statements; a conclusion follows only if it holds in every one of them.

q.e: Fix one person, then place the others using 'immediate', 'opposite' and 'second to' clues; left and right are taken from the seated person's own view (facing the centre).

q.e: Fix one person, then place the others using 'immediate', 'opposite' and 'second to' clues; left and right are taken from the seated person's own view (facing the centre).

q.e: Draw all possible Venn diagrams for the three statements; a conclusion follows only if it holds in every one of them.

q.q: A man walks 12 m towards the west. He turns right. Then he walks 15 m. He turns right. Then he walks 12 m. He turns left. Then he walks 30 m. How far is he from the starting point, and in which direction (from the starting point) is he now?
q.e: Net displacement is 0 m west and 45 m north; distance = √(0² + 45²) = 45 m.

q.q: 6 friends Bilal, Farah, Faraz, Hina, Kamran, Mariam sit in a row facing north. Bilal sits next to Farah. Kamran sits next to Faraz. Mariam sits somewhere between Kamran and Farah. Bilal sits at one of the two ends. Kamran does not sit at either end. Hina sits somewhere between Farah and Mariam. Farah sits somewhere to the left of Bilal. Who sits at the third place from the left end?
q.e: Place the definite clues first (immediate neighbours, ends), then use the 'between' and 'left of' clues to fix the rest; the arrangement is unique.

q.q: Relational Database Management System is the full form of:
q.e: Relational Database Management System is the full form of RDBMS.

q.q: The length of an IPv6 address is:
q.e: It is written in hexadecimal.

q.q: Which of the following is a symmetric encryption algorithm?
q.e: It uses the same key to encrypt and decrypt.

q.q: The HTTP status code for 'Not Found' is:
q.e: 403 means forbidden.

q.q: The HTTP status code for a successful request is:
q.e: 201 means created.

q.q: The first web browser to become widely popular was:
q.e: It was released in 1993.

q.q: The binary equivalent of the decimal number 45 is:
q.e: 32 plus 8 plus 4 plus 1.

q.q: The binary number 1010 1100 in decimal is:
q.e: 172. 128 plus 32 plus 8 plus 4.

q.q: The IEEE standard for Ethernet is:
q.e: 802.11 is Wi-Fi.

q.q: The number of usable host addresses in a /24 IPv4 network is:
q.e: Two addresses are reserved.

q.q: The technology that allows many private addresses to share one public IP is:
q.e: It conserves IPv4 addresses.

q.q: The DNS record that maps a hostname to an IPv6 address is:
q.e: AAAA. A maps to IPv4.
